prompt: Jo's monthly budget balances in most months, yet roughly four times a year Jo is suddenly overdrawn — always in months containing an annual insurance payment, a term-time travel pass, or several family birthdays. Day-to-day spending in those months is no higher than usual. What is the flaw in the budget?

options.text: Jo spends too much on small daily items, and those months are when it finally catches up
A monthly budget cannot work at all; only a weekly budget can handle real life
Jo should stop paying for insurance and travel passes, since they keep breaking the budget
The budget only plans for regular monthly costs and ignores predictable irregular ones, which should be totalled for the year, divided by twelve, and set aside monthly

explanation: The problem bills are not surprises — they arrive every year. Adding up predictable irregular costs, dividing by twelve, and putting that amount aside each month turns four crisis months into ordinary ones.
